consensus.consensusInference: The CPC's September 10 outlook raised the historic-event probability to 75% (from 69% in August): a 75% chance the 3-month RONI reaches ≥+2.5°C during Oct–Dec, which would exceed every El Niño since 1950, alongside a >90% chance of a very strong event. IRI's mid-September plume is unanimous — all 22 models (13 dynamical, 9 statistical) forecast very strong from SON 2026 through DJF, with many projecting Niño 3.4 above +3.0°C, beyond IRI's highest defined category. El Niño probability is 100% from SON 2026 through FMA 2027, with zero assigned to neutral or La Niña. The debate is settled to a single question: whether 2026 sets an outright record — and CPC now puts that at 3-in-4 on the relative index.

timeline.inference: These are official IRI probabilities that El Niño is present in each 3-month season, not its strength. El Niño probability is 100% from SON 2026 through FMA 2027, then 99% (MAM), 90% (AMJ) and 61% (MJJ 2027), with no probability assigned to neutral or La Niña through FMA. The sharp decline in spring–summer 2027 is the expected end-of-event decay — consistent with the tendency of strong events to weaken rapidly after peak — not a weakening now. Strength is at its ceiling (75% historic, >90% very strong). Both hold: near-certain through the 2026–27 winter, likely to peak at record strength, and expected to fade through 2027.
